title: Review: getting acquainted
topic: unit review: être, avoir, -er verbs, questions, c'est / il est
why: This review closes unit 1 with no new point: you combine être, avoir, -er verbs, negation, questions, c'est / il est and il y a to introduce yourself in detail and get to know someone. It is the moment to check the classic traps before moving on to daily life in unit 2.

{"lessons": ["

Introducing yourself in detail

This unit gave you everything you need to talk about yourself for a good minute. Let's put it all together. Here is a complete self-introduction, with the tool behind each sentence:

what you sayFrenchtool
nameJe m'appelle Chloé.fixed expression
ageJ'ai vingt-cinq ans.avoir + ans
nationalityJe suis française.être + agreement
cityJ'habite à Lyon.-er verb + à
jobJe suis infirmière.être + job, no article
languagesJe parle français et anglais.parler + language, no article
likesJ'aime la musique, je déteste le sport.aimer + le / la / les
what you don't doJe ne travaille pas le samedi.ne… pas

Say this little text aloud with your own details. Then try it in the third person, to introduce a friend: Elle s'appelle Chloé, elle a vingt-cinq ans, elle est infirmière… Watch the agreements if your friend is a woman.

Voici Hugo. C'est un ami. Il est canadien, il habite à Lyon et il est ingénieur.This is Hugo. He's a friend. He's Canadian, he lives in Lyon and he's an engineer.

Remember: c'est + name or article + noun, il est / elle est + adjective, job or nationality with no article.

", "

Asking: tu or vous

Getting acquainted also means asking. Choose tu with someone your age in a relaxed setting, vous with a stranger who is older, in a shop or at work. At a language exchange evening, the French usually switch to tu very quickly. When in doubt, start with vous: the other person will often say On se tutoie ? (Shall we say tu?).

with tuwith vous
nameTu t'appelles comment ?Comment vous appelez-vous ?
originTu es d'où ?Vous êtes d'où ?
cityTu habites où ?Où est-ce que vous habitez ?
ageQuel âge as-tu ?Quel âge avez-vous ?
jobTu travailles ou tu étudies ?Est-ce que vous travaillez ?
languagesTu parles combien de langues ?Quelles langues est-ce que vous parlez ?
how they are—Comment allez-vous ?

Remember the three ways of asking: a rising voice (Tu parles anglais ?), est-ce que (Est-ce que tu parles anglais ?), and the few inverted phrases you learned as they are. And to contradict a negative question, answer si.

Tu n'habites pas à Lyon ? — Si, j'habite ici !Don't you live in Lyon? — Yes, I do, I live here!

On se tutoie ? uses a verb form you'll study in unit 2: just take it as a fixed phrase. It's the friendly way to suggest using tu.

", "

Traps to avoid

Here are the mistakes English speakers make most often in this unit. Check each one before you speak:

  • Age: j'ai trente ans, never “je suis trente”.
  • Jobs: elle est médecin, never “elle est une médecin”; but c'est un médecin.
  • No “do”: Tu travailles ici ?, Je ne travaille pas. No extra verb.
  • One present: j'étudie = I study, I'm studying.
  • Gender: learn every noun with its article, la gare, le musée, l'école (f.).
  • General articles: j'aime la musique, with la, where English says “I like music”.
  • Il y a never changes: il y a des cafés.

Pronunciation reminders

The -ent of the plural is silent: ils parlent sounds like il parle. Make the liaisons: vous‿êtes, nous‿habitons, les‿amis, ils‿ont (with “z”, unlike ils sont). And don't pronounce final consonants, except c, r, f, l.

Les amis de Léa habitent à Lyon. Ils ont trente ans et ils sont anglais.Léa's friends live in Lyon. They're thirty and they're English.

Spoken French often drops the ne: je parle pas espagnol. You'll hear it all evening in a café, but write je ne parle pas espagnol.
